tests.title: Phoenix family entertainment center
tests.setup: A family entertainment business with three Phoenix-area locations. Enter all three ZIPs as locations.
tests.answer: Customers come from ZIPs with many households with children (affinity rises with the square of the share). Customer rates halve about every 7 miles from the nearest location.
tests.look: The strongest-ZIP profile should lead with households with children, kids' age groups or larger households, and the top look-alikes should be family-heavy suburbs.

tests.title: Helena, Montana farm and ranch supply
tests.setup: A rural supply store in Helena (59601) with customers spread over long distances.
tests.answer: Customers come from ZIPs with high homeownership and many households with 3+ vehicles. Customer rates halve about every 24 miles.
tests.look: Expect many ZIPs marked 'too few to judge'; that's normal for a sparse rural market. The profile should feature 3+ vehicles and homeownership.

tests.title: Atlanta tutoring service (small list)
tests.setup: A tutoring business in Brookhaven (30319) with only 150 customers.
tests.answer: Customers come from ZIPs with many college-educated adults. Customer rates halve about every 5.5 miles.
tests.look: With only 150 customers the tool uses the top-performing fifth of ZIPs for the profile. Expect education, income or home value near the top; they move together.

tests.title: Palm Beach County hearing clinic
tests.setup: A hearing clinic in Palm Beach (33480). Try 'Adults 65+' as the potential, then 'Households', and compare.
tests.answer: Customers come from ZIPs with many adults 65+ who own their homes. Customer rates halve about every 7 miles.
tests.look: With 'Households' as potential, the profile should lead with age 65+, median age or Social Security income. With 'Adults 65+' as potential, the age effect is already built into expected customers, so fewer ZIPs over-perform and homeownership stands out more.

tests.title: Dallas delivery service (no pattern)
tests.setup: A delivery business in downtown Dallas (75201).
tests.answer: There is no pattern: customers were spread purely by household count, with no distance effect.
tests.look: The tool should say distance makes little difference, mark only a handful of ZIPs over or under (chance), and label the strongest-ZIP profile as tentative.
